title: Oscar and the Deadline
premise: Sable Amberdale, a financial-crimes investigator haunted by a botched operation that killed their partner, receives a calendar invite from a handler who died a year ago — for a meeting at 9 a.m. tomorrow. When they arrive, the meeting is real: a money-laundering network spanning three governments has been using Sable's own cleared cases to move billions, and the dead handler left a dead-man's-switch trail only Sable can follow. Hunted by an assassin who is also the network's bookkeeper, and shadowed by a rival agent, Mara Voss, with whom Sable shares a fraught history, Sable must smuggle the ledger's proof to an international tribunal before the network's allies can bury it. In the climax, Sable trades the ledger's original copy — and nearly their life — to expose the final conspirator, choosing truth over the safe, clean life they once defended. The ending finds Sable testifying, sleepless still but no longer alone, having finally chosen belonging over survival.
about_author: Sebastian Halloran is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town whose banks, they insist, are entirely fictional.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Insomniac and numbed by a caseload of suspiciously clean money, Sable receives a calendar invite from Aldous Renner — their handler, dead eleven months — scheduling a meeting for tomorrow morning. The emotional beat is dread sharpened into reluctant curiosity: grief interrupted by a question that won't let go.

chapters.title: Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Flashback-tinged chapter establishing the incident that killed Renner and Sable's partner, and why Sable stopped sleeping. A routine audit flags a transaction pattern Sable has personally cleared three times before. The beat: the past isn't past; it's been signing off on their work.

chapters.title: Nine O'Clock Tomorrow
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable goes to the meeting address — an empty conference room in a Geneva satellite office — and finds a dead courier, a burned laptop, and one intact encrypted drive addressed to them. The assassin, Cassian, watches from across the street. Beat: no turning back.

chapters.title: The Bookkeeper's Knife
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. We meet the antagonist as a meticulous professional who launders by day and erases people by night, tasked with retrieving the drive. His calm is the horror. Beat: the hunter's cold competence, and his first flicker of doubt about his employers.

chapters.title: Run, Don't Walk
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable flees Geneva by train with the drive, using financial-crimes tradecraft to move untraceably. First contact with Mara Voss, an intelligence liaison who claims to be protection and might be a leash. Beat: adrenaline laced with paranoia — every helper is a suspect.

chapters.title: What Renner Left
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In a Zurich safe flat, Sable cracks the drive's first layer: Renner's private ledger linking three governments' intelligence budgets to the laundering network — and proof Sable's cleared cases were the pipeline. Beat: guilt curdling into resolve; Sable was the unwitting instrument.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Her orders are to recover the drive and contain Sable; her history with Sable complicates it. She tips them off about a border trap while reporting them contained. Beat: divided loyalty, love against duty made explicit in her choices.

chapters.title: The Vienna Cut-Out
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable and Mara meet in Vienna to copy the ledger through a data broker, who is killed minutes after the handoff. Cassian is close. Beat: the price of survival — every person who helps them becomes a target, and Sable feels each death.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Interleaved POV chapter: brief sections from officials in each of the three implicated governments, each believing they're the only one compromised. Beat: dramatic irony — the conspiracy is three men each blackmailing the others, and it's fraying.

chapters.title: Sleepless in Ljubljana
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A rare quiet night; Sable and Mara talk about Renner, about the incident, about the life Sable gave up. Almost-tenderness, interrupted by Cassian's breach. Beat: belonging offered, then weaponized — trust is the riskiest asset they hold.

chapters.title: The Tribunal Window
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Renner's dead-man's-switch reveals the final condition: the ledger must reach the international tribunal in The Hague within nine days, or its verification keys expire. Beat: the deadline becomes the book's spine; time is now a character.

chapters.title: Cassian's Ledger
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Auditing the network's books, Cassian discovers his own retirement account — his payment for a lifetime of erasures — is one of the shell structures. He is a line item. Beat: the hunter learns he is prey; his loyalty cracks.

chapters.title: The Ferry at Trieste
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A decoy handoff across the Adriatic goes wrong; Mara is captured buying Sable time to escape with the drive. Beat: sacrifice and self-loathing — Sable survives again, and survival starts to feel like a debt.

chapters.title: Interrogation, Politely
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Held by the network's most respectable conspirator, Mara is offered a deal: her career restored, Sable delivered. She negotiates, stalls, and secretly leaves a trail. Beat: love against duty — she plays both sides to protect the person she shouldn't.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Following Renner's notes, Sable finds the network's architect: not a spy or a banker, but a beloved auditor-general whose signature legitimized everything — including the operation that killed Renner. Beat: the villain revealed as banality; the incident was never an accident.

chapters.title: Nine Days to Four
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Cassian corners Sable — but instead of killing them, proposes an alliance: he'll provide the network's internal books if Sable's testimony also exposes the account that holds his money. Beat: uneasy pact; the assassin wants out, and only the truth can buy it.

chapters.title: The Hague Gambit
chapters.summary: Sable and Cassian's alternating POV. They run a financial sting — moving a marked sum through the network's own channels — to force the architect to surface before the tribunal's window closes. Beat: the hunted become hunters; competence as catharsis.

chapters.title: What Mara Did
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara escapes her captivity using the trail she planted, arriving in The Hague with evidence of her own — including a confession she extracted at real cost. Beat: her reckoning; she chooses Sable and the truth over the institution that made her.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, climax. In the tribunal's antechamber, with minutes left, the architect's allies move to seize the drive; Cassian turns his knife on his former employers; Mara holds the door. Sable uploads the ledger with seconds to spare. Beat: everything converges; the deadline met at the cost of blood.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable testifies, naming names, including their own complicity in clearing the pipeline. The architect falls; the governments scramble. Beat: truth as the only clean currency left; catharsis through accountability rather than vengeance.

chapters.title: What Survival Costs
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV, final chapter in his voice. Dissolved from the network, stripped of his accounts, Cassian disappears — leaving Sable a single line in a ledger: 'paid in full.' Beat: ambiguous mercy; even the assassin gets a form of belonging, or at least an exit.

chapters.title: Sleep, Eventually
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, resolution. Weeks later, Sable and Mara rebuild in a small coastal town; Sable takes honest, unglamorous work auditing a food bank. One morning they wake having slept through the night. Beat: quiet grace — belonging chosen, the deadline finally behind them.
